extracted.intended_audience: USPTO examiners, patent owners, third-party requesters, patent practitioners handling ex parte reexamination and copending proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on processing, merging, suspending, and otherwise handling copending ex parte reexamination proceedings and their interaction with interferences, reissue applications, and other concurrent proceedings. Covers procedural requirements, timing, required notifications, and practical examiner and practitioner obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit submissions under 37 CFR 1.565(a) to bare notice
rubrics_metrics.description: Persons making submissions under 37 CFR 1.565(a) must limit the submissions to the notification, and must not include further arguments or information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a submission is not limited to a bare notice of prior or concurrent proceedings, it will be returned, expunged or discarded by the Office. Highlighting (underlining, fluorescent marker, etc.) goes beyond bare notice. See MPEP § 2286 for Office investigation for prior or concurrent litigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper submissions under 37 CFR 1.565(a) entered into record
rubrics_metrics.description: Any proper submission pursuant to 37 CFR 1.565(a) will be promptly entered into the record of the reexamination file and considered by the examiner when the proceeding comes up for action on the merits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For example, an enterable paper from discovery in related litigation, if properly filed, will be entered and considered at the next merits action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use litigation reminder form paragraphs (22.07/22.08)
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraph 22.07 or 22.08 may be used to remind the patent owner of the continuing duty under 37 CFR 1.565(a) to apprise the Office of any litigation activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ¶ 22.07 used when granting an ex parte reexamination request filed by a patent owner and in the first action in a Director Ordered reexamination. ¶ 22.08 used when granting an ex parte reexamination request filed by a third party requester.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantial new question of patentability required for subsequent requests
rubrics_metrics.description: In order for a second or subsequent request for ex parte reexamination to be granted, a substantial new question of patentability must be raised by the art (patents and/or printed publications) cited in the second or subsequent request for reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 2240 for analysis of whether a substantial new question of patentability is raised. The second request is decided based on the claims in effect at the time of determination (37 CFR 1.515(a)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision to combine/merge made by CRU Director (or delegate)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the second or subsequent request is granted, the decision on whether or not to combine the proceedings will be made by the Central Reexamination Unit (CRU) Director where the reexamination is pending (may be delegated to CRU SPRS).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No decision on combining should be made until after reexamination is actually ordered in the later-filed request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proceedings usually merged when ex parte reexamination ordered while prior ex parte pending
rubrics_metrics.description: If ex parte reexamination is ordered while a prior ex parte reexamination proceeding is pending and prosecution in the prior proceeding has not been terminated, the ex parte reexamination proceedings will usually be merged and result in issuance and publication of a single certificate under § 1.570.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Merger rules differ for inter partes and mixed proceedings (see §§ 1.989(a),(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Office discretion to decline merger to preserve special dispatch
rubrics_metrics.description: A decision not to merge is within the sole discretion of the Office to facilitate/carry out the statutory mandate of 35 U.S.C. 305 to conduct reexamination proceedings with 'special dispatch.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If merging would unduly delay the first reexamination, the two proceedings generally will not be merged. Decisions considered case-by-case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Process second request promptly and assign to same examiner
rubrics_metrics.description: The second request should be processed as quickly as possible and assigned to the same examiner to whom the first request is assigned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If neither request has been ordered, the examiner must address each request within three months of its filing date. If Request 1 has been ordered, Request 2 should be decided immediately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not act on proceedings until statement and reply received or time expires
rubrics_metrics.description: The two proceedings should not be acted upon until the patent owner's statement and any reply by the requester have been received in Request 2, or until the time for filing same expires.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After statement/reply or expiration, the CRU Director or delegate will prepare a decision whether to merge the two proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Merged prosecution continues at most advanced point of first proceeding
rubrics_metrics.description: If the proceedings are merged, the prosecution will then continue at the most advanced point possible for the first proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a final rejection was issued in the first proceeding, prosecution will ordinarily be reopened where any new patents or publications in the second request are applied in a new ground of rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent owner gets opportunity to respond to new rejections prior to final action
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent owner will be provided with an opportunity to respond to any new rejection in a merged reexamination proceeding prior to the action being made final.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 2271 for procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Merged proceedings produce single certificate
rubrics_metrics.description: If the reexamination proceedings are merged, a single certificate will be issued based upon the merged proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 37 CFR 1.565(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Require identical claims and single duplicated responses in merged files
rubrics_metrics.description: A decision to merge should include a requirement that the patent owner maintain identical claims in both files and that responses and other papers in the merged proceeding must consist of a single response, filed in duplicate, each bearing a signature and identifying data for both files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both files will be maintained as separate complete files. If claims are not the same, the decision will give the patent owner one month to provide an amendment to make the claims the same in each file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-identical claims in merged proceedings treated as indefinite under 35 U.S.C. 112
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an amendment to make the claims the same is required by the merger decision but is not timely submitted, any claim that does not contain identical text in all merged proceedings should be rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112, second paragraph, as being indefinite.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rejection is for failure to particularly point out the invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain identical amendments while proceedings remain merged; housekeeping amendments allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: Where merger is ordered, the patent owner is required to maintain identical amendments in the merged reexamination files for the duration of the merged proceeding; if identical amendments are not present at merger, the patent owner must submit a 'housekeeping' amendment placing the same amendments in the proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Housekeeping amendments must not address any issue of patentability. Amend one or more proceedings as appropriate to achieve identical text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare single combined examiner action with both control numbers
rubrics_metrics.description: When prosecution is merged, a single combined examiner's action will be prepared; each action will contain the control number of the two proceedings on every page and a single action cover mailing sheet with both control numbers will be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support staff must ensure the action is processed and mailed to patent owner and each requester, that copies are provided, and that the entire action is scanned into the Image File Wrapper (IFW) database.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single fee in merged proceedings where fee required
rubrics_metrics.description: Where proceedings have been merged and a paper is filed which requires payment of a fee, only a single fee need be paid (e.g., excess claim fee, appeal fee), although copies must be filed for each file in the merged proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: only one appeal brief fee is required even though the brief relates to merged multiple proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: No petition to merge generally necessary; premature petitions returned
rubrics_metrics.description: No petition to merge multiple reexamination proceedings is necessary since the Office will generally, sua sponte, make a decision as to whether it is appropriate to merge; petitions to merge filed prior to determination/order will not be considered and will be returned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The decision expunging such a premature petition will be made of record in both reexamination files. See MPEP § 2267.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third-party requester limited standing to petition to merge
rubrics_metrics.description: A third party requester does not have a right to file a petition under 37 CFR 1.182 to merge a reexamination proceeding it does not have standing in; instead such a requester may file a notification of concurrent proceedings pursuant to MPEP § 2282.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Third-party requesters may petition under 37 CFR 1.182 to stay the reexamination proceeding that they requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent owner must notify Office of prior or concurrent proceedings (37 CFR 1.565)
rubrics_metrics.description: In an ex parte reexamination proceeding the patent owner must inform the Office of any prior or concurrent proceedings in which the patent is or was involved, such as interferences, reissues, other reexaminations, or litigation, and the results of such proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See also § 1.985 for notification in inter partes reexamination proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reexamination will not generally be delayed because of interference
rubrics_metrics.description: The general policy is that a reexamination proceeding will not be delayed or stayed because of an interference or possibility of an interference due to the requirement of 35 U.S.C. 305 that reexaminations be conducted with 'special dispatch.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office will make required decisions in reexamination while going forward with interference to extent desirable; Board has flexibility under 37 CFR 41.103 to tailor solutions when both copend.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interference cannot 'involve' a reexamination proceeding itself
rubrics_metrics.description: Although a patent being reexamined may be involved in an interference with an application, the reexamination proceeding itself can never be involved in an interference proceeding because a reexamination proceeding is neither an application nor a patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 35 U.S.C. 135(a) which limits interferences to applications or unexpired patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures to provoke an interference with a patent under reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: When an amendment is filed in a pending application seeking to provoke an interference with a patent involved in a reexamination, the applicant must comply with 37 CFR 41.202(a), including identifying the patent under reexamination with which interference is sought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corresponding application claims may be rejected on any applicable ground including prior art cited in the reexamination. Examiner must notify OPLA before proposing interference; interference may not be proposed unless authorized by OPLA. If interference not authorized, suspend application until reexamination certificate issued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion/request to suspend interference pending reexamination is disfavored
rubrics_metrics.description: A miscellaneous motion under 37 CFR 41.121(a)(3) to suspend an interference pending the outcome of a reexamination may be made but suspension is not favored; normally no consideration will be given unless a reexamination order has been issued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the motion under 41.121(a)(3) is denied by the administrative patent judge, a request to stay the interference may be made to the Director under 37 CFR 1.565(e). A request to stay is decided by the Chief Administrative Patent Judge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reexamination requests filed during interference processed normally; notify Board
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person may file a request for reexamination during an interference; the patent owner must notify the Board that a request for reexamination was filed within 20 days of receiving notice of the request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These requests are processed normally. No delay or stay of reexamination occurs because the requester is not a party to the interference. If examiner orders reexamination and rejects a claim corresponding to a count, the Board shall be notified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification requirements when interference declared during reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 37 CFR 1.565, the patent owner in a reexamination proceeding must notify the Office when the patent being reexamined becomes involved in an interference by filing a paper giving notice of the interference in the reexamination proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirements of 37 CFR 1.565 and 37 CFR 41.8(a) keep Office and parties informed and help eliminate procedural surprise. Parties other than the patent owner who are not requesters have limited ability to seek stays (see 1.550(g)). Premature petitions returned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board must be notified of claim changes by reexamination certificate
rubrics_metrics.description: If one or more claims of a patent involved in an interference are canceled or amended by issuance and publication of a reexamination certificate, the Board must be promptly notified and the patent owner must notify the administrative patent judge thereof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prompt notification ensures interference proceedings can account for claim changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reissue applications and ex parte reexaminations usually merged or one stayed
rubrics_metrics.description: If a reissue application and an ex parte reexamination (with an order to reexamine mailed) are pending concurrently on a patent, a decision will usually be made to merge the two proceedings or to suspend one of the two proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When merged, merged examination conducted in accordance with §§1.171–1.179 and patent owner required to place and maintain the same claims in reissue and reexamination during merged proceedings. OPLA makes decisions on merger/stay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for merger/stay decision: wait for order to reexamine and statement/reply period
rubrics_metrics.description: A decision whether to merge the reissue application examination and the ex parte reexamination, or to stay one of the proceedings, will not be made prior to the mailing of an order to reexamine pursuant to 37 CFR 1.525 and the expiration of the statement-reply period following the order to reexamine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determination on requests must be made within statutory timelines (e.g., 3 months per 35 U.S.C. 304 and 37 CFR 1.515). CRU SPRS or TC QAS await filing of any statement and reply or expiration of time, then notify OPLA for consideration of merger.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reexamination based on reissue claims when reissue issues before determination
rubrics_metrics.description: If a reissue patent issues on the patent under reexamination before determination on the reexamination request, the determination should be made on the claims of the reissue patent (the reexamination would be processed on the reissue claims rather than the original patent claims).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reissue claims used as starting point must be presented in the reexamination proceeding as a 'clean copy' (bracketed words in reissue patent claims would not appear in reexamination clean copy). Form paragraph 22.05 may be used in the Office action.
